0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
If Anjou Blanc is the entry class for dry Chenin and Saumur Blanc the continuing-education class, then Savennières is the doctoral thesis. This small AOC of only 145 hectares and the two separate crus within it — Coulée de Serrant and La Roche-aux-Moines — were praised by British wine critic Hugh Johnson as "one of the greatest dry white wines in the world."

Learning Objectives

🌋 Volcanic-rock terroir

Understand Savennières' distinctive combination of volcanic rock + schist + sand and its effect on Chenin Blanc

🏆 The trilogy: Savennières → La Roche-aux-Moines → Coulée de Serrant

Grasp the history, area, rules and stylistic progression of the three levels

🌱 Nicolas Joly and biodynamics

Know the history of Coulée de Serrant as the spiritual origin of the global biodynamic wine movement

🍷 Ageing potential and tasting technique

From tight and austere to beeswax and oxidative notes, grasp the flavour evolution of Savennières over 30 years of ageing
1.title: Savennières — The Golden Slope of the Western Loire
1.highlights.0.title: South-facing slope
1.highlights.0.content: On a south-facing slope on the north bank of the Loire, with excellent exposure, 1–2°C warmer than the surroundings
1.highlights.1.title: Airy high slopes
1.highlights.1.content: Slopes of 15–30°, with natural ventilation reducing disease risk, suited to hand cultivation
1.highlights.2.title: Three-coloured soils
1.highlights.2.content: A mix of volcanic rock (Spilite/Phtanite) + schist (Schist) + sandy alluvium (Sand)
1.content:
Savennières lies on the west side of Anjou, on a distinctive landform on the north bank of the Loire — the river makes a big bend here, with sunlight falling directly from the south on steep slopes, forming the Loire Valley's rare belt of "south-facing high slopes" (coteaux exposés sud). Not only is this slope sunny, but its soil composition is among the most complex in the Loire.

🌋 Spilite & Phtanite (volcanic rock)

From Precambrian and Cambrian submarine volcanic activity. Spilite is a pale green metamorphosed basalt, while Phtanite is an extremely hard black siliceous rock. These two rocks heat up quickly and hold heat well, giving the grapes tropical, mineral and graphite notes.

🪨 Brioverian schist

The same Precambrian schist as the bulk of Anjou, blue-grey to black, giving Chenin flint and smoky tones.

🏖️ Sandy alluvium

Sandy soil formed from Loire riverbed alluvium, concentrated at the foot of the slope, draining extremely fast and giving the wines softness.

⏳ Ageing-potential spectrum

  • 0–3 years: tight and austere, green apple, quince, lemon peel, flint, phénolique (grapefruit-pith bitterness)
  • 3–10 years: beeswax, chamomile, roasted hazelnut, mineral depth emerging, palate gradually rounding
  • 10–20 years: Madeira oxidative notes, curry, hay, candied orange peel, a foie-gras-like richness
  • 20–30+ years: mature top wines still show core acidity and complete structure (Coulée de Serrant from the 1980s is still vivid)
1.quiz.question: What is Savennières' geographic distinctiveness in the Loire Valley?
1.quiz.options.0: It lies at the source of the Loire
1.quiz.options.1: A steep south-facing slope on the north bank of the Loire, with excellent sunshine and ventilation
1.quiz.explanation: Most of the Loire Valley is gentle alluvial land, whereas Savennières lies on the north bank where the Loire makes a big bend near Angers — a position that creates a rare "steep south-facing slope" (15–30° gradient) with plenty of sun, good natural drainage and good ventilation. This distinctive landform is one of the keys to how Savennières can make top Chenin dry whites with extremely long ageing potential even in the cooler Loire climate.

3.title: The Savennières Trilogy
3.highlights.0.content: 7 hectares, sole ownership, from 1130 to today
3.highlights.2.content: The 105-hectare main AOC, the whole area
3.content:
The Savennières system expands outward into a three-tier pyramid: at the top, an extremely small single-vineyard AOC; in the middle, a Cru AOC shared among several estates; on the outside, the regional AOC. The three tiers each have their own history, winemaking rules and style.

🥇 Coulée de Serrant (single-vineyard AOC)

  • Area: 7 hectares
  • Ownership: solely owned by the Joly family since they bought it in 1962 (Domaine de la Coulée de Serrant)
  • History: planted in 1130 by Cistercian monks; through the centuries praised by King Louis XI of France and the writer Honoré de Balzac
  • Farming: fully biodynamic (Biodynamie) since the 1980s
  • Rules: yield limits stricter than the main AOC; 100% Chenin Blanc, mainly dry
  • Style: beeswax, curry, dried herbs, an extremely long finish; 30+ years of ageing potential
  • Price: €120–€200 per bottle (young wines), €300+ for aged wines

🥈 La Roche-aux-Moines (Cru AOC)

  • Area: 33 hectares
  • Ownership: shared among several estates (the largest, Domaine aux Moines, has about 9 hectares)
  • History: planted in 1106 by monks of Saint-Nicolas; named after the monastery
  • Rules: yield limits stricter than the main AOC; 100% Chenin Blanc, mainly dry
  • Style: more direct than Coulée, solidly structured, strong mineral tension
  • Role models: Domaine aux Moines, Château de Chamboureau, Domaine du Closel

🥉 Savennières (main AOC)

  • Area: about 105 hectares (after subtracting the two crus)
  • Rules: maximum dry yield 50 hL/ha; 100% Chenin Blanc, mainly dry
  • Role models: Domaine du Closel, Domaine des Baumard, Domaine du Petit Métris, Château d'Epiré
  • Style: from clean and crisp to solidly structured, depending on the estate's style

5.title: The Story of Nicolas Joly and Biodynamics
5.highlights.0.title: Change of direction in the 1980s
5.highlights.0.content: Returning from the finance industry to the family estate, fully adopting biodynamics from 1984
5.highlights.1.content: His 1997 book became the bible of the global natural-wine movement
5.highlights.2.content: Founded the international biodynamic wine organisation, with members from 16 countries and 200+ estates
5.content:
Nicolas Joly's story is a turning point in the wine world at the end of the 20th century. After returning to the family estate from New York finance at J.P. Morgan, he read Rudolf Steiner's anthroposophical agriculture writings in 1984 and boldly decided to convert Coulée de Serrant fully to biodynamics. At the time the decision was seen as madness — but 30 years later the world's top estates (DRC, Leflaive, Chapoutier and others) followed one after another, proving Joly's vision.

🌙 Core principles of biodynamics

  • Preparations 500/501: microbial activators made from cow manure packed in cow horns and buried in the soil to ferment
  • Lunar calendar: the timing of cultivation, pruning and bottling follows the Maria Thun lunar calendar
  • No synthetic chemicals: artificial fertilisers, herbicides, pesticides and added yeasts are forbidden
  • Holistic farming: the vineyard is combined with cattle, horses, chickens, bees and cover crops

🌍 The Renaissance des Appellations international organisation

The international biodynamic wine organisation founded by Joly in 2001, whose members now include:

  • France: Domaine Leflaive, Comte Lafon, Marcel Deiss, Zind-Humbrecht
  • Germany: Dr. Bürklin-Wolf, Wittmann
  • Italy: Foradori, Stella di Campalto
  • Austria: Nikolaihof, Bernhard Ott
  • 200+ estates from 16 countries hold regular touring exhibitions

📅 Nine hundred years of Savennières history — a timeline

1106
🙏 La Roche-aux-Moines founded

Monks of Saint-Nicolas cleared the vineyard here, establishing one of the oldest ecclesiastical vineyards on the western Loire

1130
🏛️ Coulée de Serrant founded

Cistercian monks began planting; through the centuries praised by King Louis XI and the writer Balzac, with continuous planting for over 900 years

1984
🌱 The biodynamic revolution

Nicolas Joly read the anthroposophical writings of Rudolf Steiner and fully converted Coulée de Serrant, regarded by the trade as "an act of madness"

1997
📚 "Wine from Sky to Earth" published

It became the foundational work of the global natural-wine and biodynamic farming movement, its influence reaching top estates such as DRC and Leflaive

2000s
🌍 Renaissance des Appellations grows

200+ estates from 16 countries joined, bringing Savennières' biodynamic philosophy to the global wine stage
5.quiz.question: By whose writings was Nicolas Joly inspired to convert Coulée de Serrant to biodynamics in 1984?
5.quiz.explanation: Nicolas Joly was inspired by Rudolf Steiner's (1861–1925) 1924 "Agriculture Course." Steiner was an Austrian philosopher and founder of anthroposophy, who proposed treating a farm as an organic whole and introduced concepts such as lunar phases, the movement of the stars and special preparations. Steiner's theories became the foundation of global biodynamic agriculture (the Demeter certification system), though long regarded by mainstream agronomy as "mysticism." Joly is one of the few pioneers to have put them fully into practice at the level of top wine.
6.title: Level 3-2 Knowledge Check
6.questions.0.question: What are the area and ownership of Coulée de Serrant?
6.questions.0.options.1: 7 hectares, solely owned by the Joly family
6.questions.0.explanation: Coulée de Serrant is a very rare Loire "single vineyard + single owner AOC" (similar to Burgundy's Romanée-Conti). At only 7 hectares, it has been run solely by the Joly family since they bought it in 1962. This structure lets the estate fully control style and quality, a very special case in the French AOC system.
6.questions.1.question: Which two rocks mainly make up the volcanic rock in the Savennières AOC?
6.questions.1.explanation: Spilite is a pale green metamorphosed basalt (Precambrian), and Phtanite is an extremely hard black siliceous rock. Both formed in Precambrian to Cambrian submarine volcanic activity and are key components of Savennières terroir. They heat up quickly and hold heat well, giving the grapes tropical, mineral and graphite notes, and are the biggest difference between Savennières and the bulk of Anjou Blanc (pure schist).
6.questions.2.question: What is the hierarchy of the Savennières pyramid from the inside out?
6.questions.2.explanation: From the top (smallest, strictest) to the broadest: Coulée de Serrant (7 hectares, single-vineyard AOC) → La Roche-aux-Moines (33 hectares, Cru AOC) → Savennières (105-hectare main AOC, dry 50 hL/ha). This structure is similar to Burgundy's Grand Cru → Premier Cru → Village logic.
6.questions.3.question: After 20 years of ageing, which aroma tones most commonly appear in top Savennières?
6.questions.3.options.1: Beeswax, curry, Madeira oxidative notes, hay
6.questions.3.explanation: The signature aroma evolution of aged top dry Chenin Blanc: the green apple, quince and lemon peel of youth gradually develop into beeswax, roasted hazelnut, curry (fenugreek/sotolon), Madeira oxidative notes, hay and candied orange peel. This aromatic range differs from Riesling and top old Chardonnay, and is Chenin's own "ageing fingerprint," the key to identifying old Savennières / Vouvray Sec.
